v.q: What happens when a let variable is read before its declaration?
v.w: The variable is in the temporal dead zone until its line runs.
The object it holds can still change unless it is frozen.

v.q: What does a closure keep alive?
o: The scope where the function was created
v.w: A function carries the lexical scope around it, even after the outer function returned.

v.q: Why do var callbacks in a loop all print the final value?
v.w: let creates a new binding per iteration, which fixes it.

v.q: What is this in a plain function call in strict mode?
v.w: There is no object before the dot, so strict mode leaves this undefined.

v.q: Which function type uses the this of its enclosing scope?
v.w: Arrow functions have no this of their own, and call or bind cannot change it.

v.q: What does the engine do when a property is not found on an object?
v.w: The lookup walks the prototype chain until it finds the key or reaches null.

v.q: What is the class keyword in JavaScript?
v.w: Methods go on Class.prototype and extends links two prototypes.

v.q: What does the spread operator copy for an object?
v.w: Nested objects stay shared, so spread makes a shallow copy.

v.q: Which built-in makes a deep copy, including dates and cycles?
v.w: It cannot copy functions. JSON round trips lose dates, undefined and functions.

v.q: Which array method returns a sorted copy without changing the original?
v.w: The newer methods toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced and with return copies.

v.q: Why can bundlers tree-shake ES modules?
v.w: Static imports can be analysed before the code runs, so unused exports are removed.

v.q: Which module system uses require and module.exports?
v.w: It loads synchronously at run time and is common in older Node.js code.
